run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: The orca workload in namespace app-95 is failing because its single container repeatedly exceeds its 128Mi memory limit and is OOM-killed. Observed on the only pod, orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k (owner ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, owner Deployment orca): the container last terminated with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137 at 16:43:12Z (restartCount 1 at that time), and by 16:43:54Z a second OOMKill had been recorded (exit 137, finished 16:43:41Z) with the pod Running but ready=false. The application's own logs show monotonic, unbounded retention: in the current container instance the reported approximate stored-image memory rose from 9.0 MB at 10 processed images to 112.5 MB at 90 images (about 1.3 MB per image) while printing 'Cache size: N thumbnails' and 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items', then it stopped right after 'Processing image 96' and was OOM-killed. Logs also state 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval'. The Deployment sets limits.memory=128Mi and requests.memory=64Mi, and the observed growth crosses that 128Mi cap at roughly 95-100 images in each ~28 second run. Node and cluster level alternatives were checked: node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports MemoryPressure=False with 32859952Ki allocatable, there is no ResourceQuota in app-95, there is no sidecar container, and no Evicted/Unhealthy event exists for the pod - so this is a container cgroup-limit OOM, not node pressure or eviction. I fetched and worked through runbook python-memory-troubleshooting: step 1 (application status) was carried out with kubernetes_jq_query on pods/deployments; step 2 (logs) with fetch_pod_logs, which showed the memory/cache/processed lines and the OOM boundary but no memory/GC ERROR or WARNING lines in the 200 lines shown; step 3 (code patterns) was carried out against logs only, because the application code lives in Secret orca-app mounted at /app and secrets cannot be read; step 4 (growth patterns) was carried out from the log-reported estimates, but 'kubectl top' is not available in this Run; step 5 (memory metrics/limits) was only partly carried out - limits were read from the pod/deployment spec (128Mi/64Mi), but Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so no container memory or restart metric series were obtained; the py-spy / exec / debug-endpoint steps could not be carried out because no exec tool is available. orca is a brand-new workload (Deployment revision 1, ReplicaSet and pod created 16:42:43Z), so no pre-incident baseline for its memory behaviour exists in the window. Root cause named below is the Deployment object that carries the 128Mi limit against which the app's unbounded in-process retention collides; the deeper application-level retention code is a hypothesis because it lives in an unreadable Secret.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k in namespace app-95 is owned by ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f and runs the single container 'orca' (image python:3.9-slim) with limits.memory=128Mi and requests.memory=64Mi.

The pod's container last terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 (finished 16:43:12Z, started 16:42:44Z) with restartCount 1; at that observation the pod was phase Running and ready=true because the container had just been restarted at 16:43:13Z.

A second OOMKill occurred: at 16:43:54Z pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k was phase Running but ready=false, the container state was terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled finished at 16:43:41Z, and the previous termination was OOMKilled/137 at 16:43:12Z.

Application logs of the previous container instance show monotonic growth of in-memory retention: 'Approximate memory used by stored images' 25.0 MB at 20 images, 36.6 MB at 30, 47.7 MB at 40, 61.3 MB at 50, 74.8 MB at 60, 88.4 MB at 70, 98.7 MB at 80 and 112.5 MB at 90 images, each accompanied by 'Cache size: N thumbnails' and 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items'; the last line before the OOMKill was 'Processing image 96' at 16:43:12.789788Z.

The restarted container instance logs 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval' at 16:43:13.95Z and again repeats the same growth pattern (9.0 MB at 10 images, 22.7 MB at 20, 37.2 MB at 30, 48.4 MB at 40, 60.2 MB at 50), reaching 'Processing image 53' at 16:43:20.57Z before the 16:43:41Z OOMKill.

Deployment orca in app-95 carries container resource limits.memory=128Mi and requests.memory=64Mi, runs command python /app/app.py with volumeMount /app from volume 'app-code' backed by secretName orca-app, environment SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor; deployment.kubernetes.io/revision is 1 and the object was last applied by manager kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-23T16:42:43Z, with status availableReplicas=1 and readyReplicas=1.

The ownership chain is Deployment orca -> ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f (created 2026-11-23T16:42:43Z, replicas 1, readyReplicas 1) -> the single pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k (startTime 2026-11-23T16:42:43Z); only one ReplicaSet exists, so no older ReplicaSet was replaced by this rollout.

Events for pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k in the window are all Normal: Scheduled (16:42:43Z), Pulled (count 2), Created (count 2), Started (count 2, last 16:43:13Z); no OOMKilling, Killing, Unhealthy or Failed event was returned for that pod. Cluster-wide grouping shows only 6 events in total: Deployment/app-95 ScalingReplicaSet, Pod/app-95 Created, Pulled, Scheduled, Started, and ReplicaSet/app-95 SuccessfulCreate.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports MemoryPressure=False (reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory), Ready=True and allocatable memory 32859952Ki, so the OOMKills are not explained by node-level memory pressure.

No ResourceQuota objects exist in namespace app-95 at query time (the resourcequotas query processed 0 items), and the only ConfigMap in app-95 is kube-root-ca.crt - there is no application ConfigMap holding the 'store all processed images' / 'cache thumbnails' settings; the application code is mounted from secretName orca-app.

Node-level memory pressure was checked and rejected as a cause: the node hosting the pod has MemoryPressure=False and 32859952Ki allocatable memory, while the container was killed at its own 128Mi cgroup limit.

Eviction or a Failed/Unhealthy pod condition was considered and not supported: the pod shows a container restart in place with last termination reason OOMKilled, and no Evicted, Killing, Unhealthy or Failed event exists for it in the window.
A sidecar or second container consuming memory was considered and not supported: the pod spec and status list only the single container 'orca'.

The deepest cause indicated by the logs is unbounded in-process retention in the orca application - a growing 'processed_images' list plus a thumbnail cache with no eviction ('Storing all processed images for audit trail', 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval') - at roughly 1.3 MB per image, which crosses the 128Mi container limit at about 95-100 images in each ~28 second run. The code itself lives in Secret orca-app and could not be read, so this retention configuration could not be verified in source.

Treat this as a recurring OOM loop rather than a one-off: raise the container memory limit (and matching request) above the observed peak, or cap retention - bounded cache/collections.deque(maxlen) or TTL eviction, and stream/offload the audit trail instead of keeping every processed image in memory - then verify with the pod's restart count and memory working set.

Instrument the process to expose runtime memory (tracemalloc/RSS) and enable Prometheus scraping of the pod, because the only memory figures available in this Run are the application's own log estimates; also confirm the retention settings inside Secret orca-app and whether the audit-trail retention is intentional.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query (twice) and get_series all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no container_memory_working_set_bytes, restart-counter or kube-state-metrics series were obtained; memory-vs-limit over time and any metric-based baseline are unknown, not zero.
No 'kubectl top'-style live memory reading is available as a tool, so the only growth figures are the application's log-reported approximations ('Approximate memory used by stored images').

Secret orca-app (mounted at /app) holds the application code and could not be read, so the retention/leak code path and the meaning of the 'Storing all processed images' setting could not be verified.

No OOMKilling or Killing event was recorded for pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ljz6k; the OOM evidence is the container's lastState reason/exit code (137) only, and the 6 events returned cover just 16:42:43Z-16:43:13Z, so events after that are unknown.

Traces could not be used: traces_search for service 'orca' returned INVALID_PARAMS because orca is not among the Jaeger service names, and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so orca's instrumentation status and any trace-level view are unknown.

Change history is an integration not configured for this Run, so what changed at 2026-11-23T16:42:43Z (when Deployment orca revision 1 and its ReplicaSet/pod were created) cannot be traced beyond metadata.managedFieldsSummary showing kubectl-client-side-apply.
Pod state after 2026-11-23T16:43:54Z is unknown, including whether the OOM/restart loop continues or whether the pod eventually reaches a stable state.
No pre-incident baseline for orca exists in the window: the Deployment, ReplicaSet and pod were all created at 16:42:43Z, so there are no earlier memory or restart readings to compare against.
next_steps: Read Secret orca-app (mounted at /app) with an authorized operator to confirm the retention code and whether 'Storing all processed images for audit trail' / 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval' are unbounded, per the fetched runbook's code-pattern step.
Run 'kubectl top pod -n app-95 -l app=orca' and, if the image supports it, py-spy dump or a tracemalloc snapshot in the container to quantify which structures hold the ~1.3 MB per processed image.

Configure Prometheus scraping / container memory metrics for namespace app-95 so future investigations have container_memory_working_set_bytes and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total rather than log estimates alone.
Verify whether a kubelet OOMKilling event is emitted later for this pod (node event retention) to corroborate the cgroup-limit kill independently of container lastState.

Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
